what_its_for: Patiromer is used to lower high potassium levels in your blood (a condition called hyperkalemia). Too much potassium in your blood can be dangerous and cause serious heart problems. This medicine works in your gut by trapping extra potassium and removing it from your body through your stool.
how_to_take: Mix the powder with about 1/3 cup (approximately 80 mL) of water. Stir well and drink right away. If powder remains in the glass, add more water, stir, and drink again. Make sure you take the full dose. Take patiromer with food. Do NOT heat the powder or mix it with hot liquids. Do NOT take it dry. Take patiromer at least 3 hours before or 3 hours after taking other oral medications, since it can affect how other medicines are absorbed.
dosing: The usual starting dose is one packet (8.4 grams) taken once daily with food. Your doctor may increase your dose over time based on your blood potassium levels. The maximum dose is three packets (25.2 grams) per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store unopened packets in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). If needed, you may store unopened packets at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 6 months. Do not return packets to the refrigerator once they have been stored at room temperature. Keep packets away from heat and moisture. Once mixed with water, use the mixture right away and do not store it for later. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not take other oral medications within 3 hours before or 3 hours after taking patiromer, as it can prevent your other medicines from working properly. Always check with your pharmacist or doctor about timing your other medications. Do not mix the powder with hot food or liquids. Do not eat a high-potassium diet (such as large amounts of bananas, oranges, potatoes, or salt substitutes) without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: severe constipation or no bowel movements for several days, severe stomach pain, nausea or vomiting that does not go away, signs of low potassium such as muscle weakness, muscle cramps, irregular heartbeat, or unusual tiredness, or any signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if you notice swelling in your hands, ankles, or feet, as patiromer contains some sodium.
when_it_works: Patiromer starts working within a few hours of taking your first dose. Most people see a meaningful drop in their blood potassium levels within the first week of treatment. Your doctor will check your blood potassium levels regularly to make sure the medicine is working and to adjust your dose if needed. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you have a history of bowel problems, constipation, or recent bowel surgery, as patiromer may worsen constipation. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, talk to your doctor before taking this medicine. It is not known if patiromer passes into breast milk, so discuss breastfeeding with your doctor. This medicine has not been well studied in children, so talk to your doctor about safety if this is for a child. Older adults (age 65 and over) can generally take this medicine but should be monitored closely for constipation and low potassium levels.
